extracted.intended_audience: Indian groups petitioning for federal acknowledgement; Bureau of Indian Affairs / Department of the Interior staff; tribal advocates and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative procedures and substantive criteria (Part 54 draft) for establishing that an American Indian group exists as an Indian tribe, including definitions, required petition contents, evidentiary presumptions, processing timelines, notices, and appeal/decision procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Indian Tribe' / 'Tribe'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Indian Tribe" also referred to herein as "tribe" means any Indian group within the United States that the Secretary of Interior acknowledges to be an Indian tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the operative definition for eligibility for acknowledgement and for determining which groups fall under these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — which groups this part covers / excludes
rubrics_metrics.description: This part is intended to cover only those American Indian groups which may have the attributes of Indian Tribes, but which have not as yet been fully acknowledged as such by the Department. It is not intended to apply to associations, organizations, corporations, or groups composed of individuals descended from many groups unless there has been a historic association such that they functioned as a single entity for a protracted period. Nor is it intended to apply to splinter groups, political factions, communities or groups which separated from the main body of an acknowledged tribe unless it can be clearly established that the group has functioned historically and for a protracted period as an autonomous entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this scope to screen petitions; splinter groups must show historical autonomous functioning to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Indian group in the United States which believes it should be acknowledged as an Indian tribe, and can satisfy the criteria in Section 54.7, may submit a petition requesting that the Secretary acknowledge the group's existence as an Indian Tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing entitlement is broad but conditioned on ability to meet the substantive criteria in 54.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department duties to contact and assist groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Department shall contact, within a twelve-month period following enactment, all known Indian tribal groups in the United States whose existence has not been previously acknowledged and shall inform them of their right to petition. The Department shall also provide, to the fullest extent possible, technical assistance to the petitioning group in investigating the group's historical background and Indian identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOI/BIA have affirmative outreach and assistance obligations; failure to notify or assist could be relevant to fairness of process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and availability of petition guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Within sixty (60) days after publication of final regulations, the Secretary will have available suggested guidelines for the format of the petition, including general suggestions on where and how to research for required information and examples of acceptable documents. Examples shall not preclude use of any other format or acceptable document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may follow suggested formats but may also submit other acceptable documentation; guidance will be published and available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: Statement of longstanding Indian identity
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of facts establishing that the group has been identified as 'Indian, Native American, or aboriginal' for a protracted period of time. Longstanding Indian identity may include identification as a division/combination/confederation with other tribes if not in conflict with other criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence includes but is not limited to: (i) repeated identification by federal authorities; (ii) long-standing relationships with state governments based on identification as the group as Indian; (iii) repeated dealings with county/parish/local government; (iv) identification as Indian in courthouse, church, or school records; (v) identification as Indian by anthropologists/historians or other scholars; (vi) identification as Indian in newspapers and books; (vii) any other relevant evidence deemed by the Office of the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: Governing documents or membership criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the group's present governing document(s), or in the absence of a written document, a statement describing in full the membership criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where tribal governance is informal, a clear description of traditional/actual decision-making structures must be provided; definitions emphasize understanding governance in the context of Indian culture and social organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: Lists of current and former members and membership descent standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of all current members of the group and a copy of each available former list of members. Membership must consist of individuals who have established, using evidence acceptable to the Secretary, descent from a common tribal origin which existed historically or tribal origins with a known historic relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable membership evidence includes (i) membership rolls approved by the Secretary for prior federal purposes; (ii) state, federal or other official records identifying members or ancestors as Indian; (iii) church, school enrollment records indicating membership; (iv) newspaper or similar evidence; (v) reputation in the community or among tribal members; (vi) any other record or evidence identifying the person as a member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: No Congressional termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning group is not, nor are its members, the subject of Congressional legislation which has expressly terminated the federal relationship between the applicant group and the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior act of Congressional termination disqualifies the group from acknowledgement under these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: Composition not principally a splinter group
rubrics_metrics.description: The membership of the petitioning group is composed principally of persons who are not a splinter group or political faction from the main body of a tribe currently acknowledged as an Indian tribe by the Department, unless it can be established that the group has functioned for a protracted period as an autonomous entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups claiming to be offshoots of an acknowledged tribe must produce strong historical evidence of autonomous functioning to overcome presumption of being a splinter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary presumption: party to a treaty or successor in interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning group has been a party to a treaty or agreement with the United States or is a successor in interest to an Indian tribe which treated with or had an agreement ratified by Congress. For these purposes, 'successor in interest' means an Indian group whose members are principally descendants of the tribe in question and which has evolved from the tribe and maintained a tribal structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One such factor creates a presumption the group is eligible for acknowledgement; evidence supporting treaty-party status is highly probative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary presumption: party to unratified treaty or treaty negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning group has been a party to or successor in interest to an Indian tribe which was either a party to an unratified treaty or agreement with the United States, or entered treaty negotiations with the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historic participation in treaty negotiations or unratified treaties supports acknowledgement presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary presumption: party to treaty/agreement with foreign/colonial government
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning group was a party to or successor in interest to an Indian tribe which was a party to a treaty or agreement with a foreign nation or colonial government, the obligations and rights of such treaty being assumed by the United States upon acquisition of land areas where the petitioning group historically resided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historic international/colonial treaties affecting the group's rights can create a presumption of tribal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary presumption: prior formal governmental designation or court acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning group or its historic predecessor has been designated a tribe by an act of Congress, Executive Order, denoted as a tribe in the legislative history of a bill which was enacted into law, or has been acknowledged to be a tribe by a court of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any prior formal governmental or judicial designation as a tribe is highly persuasive evidence for acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary presumption: considered by state or federal agency as an Indian entity with collective rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The group has been considered by a state or by an agency of the federal government as an Indian entity having collective rights in land/water/funds or other assets, or having collective hunting and fishing rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative recognition by other government agencies of the group's collective rights supports a presumption of tribal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary presumption: recognition by other tribes / nearby communities
rubrics_metrics.description: The group is viewed as a distinct Indian group by other tribes or by the members of nearby communities. This may be evidenced by written statements from presently acknowledged tribes or referring communities stating that they have related to the unacknowledged group for purposes connected with intertribal activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intertribal recognition is a relevant factor and may be evidenced by documented intertribal interactions or statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation standard favorable to petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Any one of the evidentiary items listed shall create a presumption that the petitioning group is a tribe eligible for acknowledgement and all other evidence submitted shall be interpreted in a light favorable to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are instructed to construe ambiguous evidence in favor of the petitioner when assessing tribal existence under these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of receipt and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten (10) days after receiving a petition, the Assistant Secretary shall send an acknowledgment of receipt in writing to the petitioner, and shall publish in the Federal Register a notice of such receipt including the name, location, and mailing address of the petitioning group and where the petition may be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely public notice is mandatory and must include sufficient identifying information and access instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing review and deficiency notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a petition the Assistant Secretary shall cause a review to determine whether the group is entitled to acknowledgement, including consideration of petition and supporting evidence and verification as necessary. Within thirty (30) days after publication of notice of receipt, the Assistant Secretary shall notify the petitioning group of any obvious deficiencies or significant omissions apparent on initial review and may suggest actions for conformance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners receive early, specific notice of deficiencies and may be guided on how to cure them; timelines begin with publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority / first-come, first-served rule and amendment option
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions shall be considered on a first come, first serve basis determined by the date of original filing with the Department. Petitioning groups with petitions already on file at enactment may choose to amend their petitions or file entirely new ones; withdrawing an already filed petition shall not cause loss of priority date if they later resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority preservation rules protect earlier filers; bureaus must track original filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when petition under active consideration and access to staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall be notified when the petition comes under active consideration and who the primary Bureau staff member reviewing the petition is (and back-up and supervisor). Notice shall include office address and telephone number. During review, the petitioning group shall be provided copies of all additional documents, letters and other evidence obtained or received by the Bureau's staff relevant to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and direct staff contact required; petitioner entitled to all evidence collected relevant to their case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for proposed findings and possible extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall publish his proposed findings in the Federal Register within one (1) year after notifying the petitioner that active consideration has begun. The Secretary may extend that period up to an additional 180 days upon a showing that the petitioner has contributed to delay by failing to cure significant omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-year target for proposed findings; extensions limited and tied to petitioner's contribution to delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary findings and petitioner's rebuttal opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall make a preliminary report to the petitioner of proposed findings and conclusions, outlining the evidence for the decision. Upon receipt, the petitioner shall have ninety (90) days to respond, including an opportunity to present oral argument to rebut the evidence relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner has a formal written and oral opportunity to rebut before final determination; 90-day rebuttal window is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action, Secretary review, and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall have thirty (30) days after petitioner's response to prepare a report of findings and final determination and publish it in the Federal Register. The Assistant Secretary's final determination shall be subject to review by the Secretary, who may, by acting within thirty (30) days of such publication, supersede that determination. If the Secretary takes no action within such 30-day period, the Assistant Secretary's determination shall be final and effective as of the date of publication. The petitioner shall have the right to present its own response to the Secretary concerning the Assistant Secretary's final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finality process includes short Secretary review window; publication date controls effective date; petitioner allowed to respond to Secretary if review is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal procedure and alternative options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Assistant Secretary refuses to acknowledge the petitioning group as an Indian tribe, he shall within thirty (30) days after such refusal analyze and forward to the petitioner other options (if any) under which application for services and other benefits may be made. Such options shall include legislation or possible membership in an already acknowledged Indian tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refused petitioners must be given a written analysis and practical options for obtaining services or recognition via alternative routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of acknowledgement — eligibility and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determination that the petitioner is an Indian tribe, the tribe shall be fully eligible for all services and benefits from the federal government available to other federally acknowledged tribes and entitled to all the privileges and immunities available to other federally acknowledged tribes by reason of their sovereign status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement confers full eligibility for federal services, benefits, and sovereign privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding protection obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall take all steps necessary to ensure appropriation(s) for BIA programs and services if that assistance and services to existing tribes will not be diminished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department must plan to avoid diminishing services to existing tribes when new tribes are acknowledged; petitioners are encouraged to specify projected financial burdens to enable Congressional planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to specify financial impact in petitioning for recognition (advisory provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a tribe is petitioning for recognition they should specify the financial burden that this will be placing on the United States so that Congress and other funding authorities can plan for the increased budget without diminishing services to previously recognized tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners are advised (and may be required by policy) to include estimated financial impacts to facilitate appropriations planning and avoid unplanned service diminishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and evidentiary understanding of 'autonomous' tribal structure
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Autonomous' means having a separate tribal council, structure or other organizational mechanism that the group uses as its own means of making group decisions (such as determination of membership). The tribal structure must be understood in the context of the Indian culture and social organization of that group; many acknowledged tribes possess informal leadership structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators must consider cultural forms of governance and not reject groups for lacking formal written constitutions if traditional or informal institutions perform governing functions.
